checkpoint_review: The Router correctly identified that most anatomical checkpoints (Head, Limbs, Ventral scales) are untestable due to the subject being partially submerged. I agree with marking these as 'N/A' rather than 'Missing', as the occlusion is environmental (water) rather than a generation failure. The Router was correct to mark the dorsal scute texture and elongated body as present and testable. The expert classifier confirms the species identity (Nile Crocodile) with high confidence despite the partial view, validating the alignment of the visible features.
artifact_review: The Router identified a texture anomaly on the right object (smooth/melted appearance). I agree this is a notable defect; it lacks the distinct osteoderm definition of the left object and resembles a log or melted geometry more than a crocodile back. The topology auditor's mask shows fragmentation at the edges of the right object, supporting the 'structural collapse/melting' assessment at the water interface. The perceptual auditor noted slight compression, which aligns with the lack of fine detail in the water ripples. The severity of the right object's artifact is significant enough to lower the artifact score, as it introduces ambiguity about whether it is a second animal or debris.
alignment_reasoning: High alignment for visible features. Expert classifier strongly confirms Nile Crocodile. Uncheckable points are legitimately occluded by water, not missing from generation. Visible dorsal texture matches target class perfectly.
artifact_reasoning: Right-side object exhibits texture melting and lack of scute definition compared to the left. Water-subject boundary ambiguity on right object. Slight compression detected. The ambiguity of the right object prevents a perfect artifact score.
